event.description: Date: Oct 1st Time: 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM Location: 1107 Fulton St. ZARTONK Gallery Armenian Cultural Month Celebration in cooperation with Downtown Fresno Partnership @ Mariposa Plaza. Landscape Memories, latitude 36.74773 / longitude 119.77237 (Fresno, CA) On October 1, 2026, in Fresno, Antaramian Hofman exhibits the final artistic display of migratory footprints by way of dance and people gatherings. Artist Hazel Antaramian Hofman is recognized for her ‘artwork of traces’: art and writing that looks to movement and pathway as conceptual anchor points of expression. The unknowingness of where you have been and where you are going is intrinsic to the movement of her pencil or the strokes of her paintbrush. Born in Armenia, now in Fresno, the pathway in between includes Moscow, Paris, New York, Boston, Madison, Kenosha, Milwaukee. For her, geographic coordinates share spaces with those who traverse them and those who document them. In Spring 2026, Antaramian completed Step 2 of her project. A three-generation family of dancers in the Armenian tradition: Karine Nurijanyan, Anna Dolukhanyan, and Ani Sargsyan led viewer participants in an Armenian traditional dance placing their inked footprint upon the floored canvas as it served to cushion their trac es of the event, the memory to come between themselves and the earth landscape. It became a marking of language and the line folk dance; all aimed at connection. The traces of footprints and handprints are embedded further with the overlaid painting of Step 3 of Antaramian’s project, continuing to mark human physicality. A physicality that speaks to theindividual and the collective. Antaramian’s artistic and performance art traces are shared with other art motifs, such as birds, the sky, nondescript land, dystopic patterns, and shoes. The symbolic language of these motifs are terrestrial longings for flight.
